articles.headline: Downtown security officers begin strike
articles.summary: Security guards began striking at Salesforce Tower, the Transbay transit center and other downtown properties on September 18. The Chronicle reported an impasse in contract negotiations.

articles.headline: Front Street hosts Oktoberfest
articles.summary: A free downtown Oktoberfest celebration ran September 18 with music, food and games.

articles.headline: Mountain lion captured in Outer Sunset
articles.summary: City officials captured a mountain lion on September 18 after sightings near 44th Avenue and Ulloa Street, according to The San Francisco Standard.

articles.headline: California gasoline reaches $6 a gallon
articles.summary: The Chronicle reported a statewide average of $6 per gallon on September 14 and a San Francisco average of $6.16, citing AAA. Statewide prices had risen 42 cents over the preceding month.

articles.headline: Raising Cane’s announces first San Francisco opening
articles.summary: Raising Cane’s announced plans to open at 211 Jefferson Street at Fisherman’s Wharf on September 21. The September 14 report describes a planned opening, not an already operating restaurant.

articles.headline: Dreamforce brings conference activity to downtown
articles.summary: A September 14 Chronicle report previewed Dreamforce at Moscone Center for September 15–17 and described a 50,000-person conference. That figure is the reported conference size, not verified foot traffic or restaurant demand.

articles.headline: Hi NRG opens permanent coffee shop in San Francisco's Richmond
articles.summary: The Richmond District coffee pop-up has opened a permanent space serving food, wine and beer alongside music.

articles.headline: KEXP plans music hub at San Francisco's Haight-Ashbury
articles.summary: KEXP was selected to help turn a Haight-Ashbury site into a music venue with broadcasts, performances and classes.

articles.headline: Uber plans 253 layoffs at San Francisco headquarters
articles.summary: State filings outline 390 planned Bay Area job cuts at Uber, including 253 at its San Francisco headquarters.

articles.headline: BART delays ease after plastic debris fire near 24th Street Mission
articles.summary: Burning plastic on the tracks near 24th Street Mission caused major delays on September 17; service subsequently improved.

articles.headline: San Francisco film production surges 28% amid new film incentives
articles.summary: A new report puts film and television production up 28% in the latest fiscal year, with local spending reaching $32.3 million.

articles.headline: San Francisco Opera and orchestra reach tentative deal to end strike
articles.summary: The opera company and its orchestra reached a provisional contract agreement after a strike disrupted performances.

articles.headline: Sutro Hall to fill empty restaurant space in historic SF building
articles.summary: Restaurant veterans plan to open Sutro Hall in the vacant restaurant space at 140 New Montgomery downtown.

articles.headline: First look at downtown San Francisco's proposed 910-foot office tower
articles.summary: New renderings show the proposed Fifty at First office tower, planned to stand 910 feet tall in downtown San Francisco.

articles.headline: Athleta launches partnership with Golden State Valkyries
articles.summary: Athleta announced a multiyear partnership with the Golden State Valkyries basketball team.

articles.headline: Melanie C to perform at Castro Theatre before Portola festival debut
articles.summary: Melanie C announced a Castro Theatre performance ahead of her DJ debut at the Portola Music Festival.

articles.headline: Highway 101 weekend closure planned for repair work
articles.summary: Caltrans plans to close a stretch of Highway 101 in San Francisco for weekend repairs, according to KTVU.

articles.headline: State funding planned for legal help for domestic violence survivors
articles.summary: The Standard reports that California is poised to provide $1.5 million for free legal representation for domestic violence survivors through the city’s Mayor’s Office for Victims’ Rights.

articles.headline: Noe Valley running store hit by another burglary
articles.summary: CBS reports that burglars stole shoes and clothing from a Noe Valley running store, its fourth break-in in less than two years.

articles.headline: Former employee files discrimination lawsuit against SF Standard
articles.summary: Mission Local reports allegations of gender discrimination and harassment in a lawsuit against the San Francisco Standard and its CEO. These are allegations, not findings.

articles.headline: Four arrested in investigation following teen’s fatal overdose
articles.summary: Police arrested four people and seized 20,000 pills in a San Francisco investigation following a teenager’s fatal overdose, according to KMPH.

articles.headline: Lowriding celebration takes over Mission Street
articles.summary: An Associated Press report describes drivers cruising along Mission Street to celebrate San Francisco’s lowriding culture.

articles.headline: Developers propose basketball complex at SF Centre mall
articles.summary: The Standard reports that Urban Land Development and TMG Partners submitted a bid for San Francisco Centre with a basketball-focused proposal.
